summary: Selected the cross-review-surviving generic quaternion-product specialization (Fable 1 / Pro 2) and applied the reviewers' enlarged-kernel correction to its smallest frozen 4x2 seam. The labels a=(0,1,u,1+u), b=(0,1) over Z[u]/(u^2-3) give nonzero mod-17 tags to all six tested old transportation quadratics and to the false-111 coefficient vector in both COPY orientations. Exact enumeration of all 3^8 coefficient vectors in {-1,0,1}^8 nevertheless finds a conformally primitive signed move of L1 and squared coefficient weight 8 with zero row margins, column margins, and product tag over Z, hence also modulo 17 and 289. This is only a finite kill of that label specialization; it is not CVP-energy evidence and does not settle other O/P^2 assignments, Q1, Q2, or any asymptotic claim.
hypothesis: Genuine product tags can move Q1 only if separation survives recomputation of the enlarged signed kernel: passing each old primitive individually is insufficient because their transfers can cancel in a new low-weight pair-selector move. The discriminating falsification condition is an exact nonzero signed all-pairs move with zero old margins and zero product transfer after the named old moves pass.

tests.finding: The frozen specialization detects all six tested old 4x2 quadratics and false 111, but exactly two bounded enlarged-kernel moves (one up to sign) survive; the witness has coefficient L1=8, squared coefficient weight=8, and exact tag (0,0).
The new deterministic verifier compiles as Python.
